title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 73–75). Grothendieck is building an axiomatic 'analysis situs'. He works with a class 𝓕 of 'figures' carrying three relations:
- ≤ : 'is a sub-figure of';
- ≼ : apparently 'is a subdivision of';
- a disjointness or compatibility relation.
These are governed by axioms C1–C7. On p. 73 he defines refinement: G ≪ F iff there is F' with G ≤ F' ≼ F. He wants to show that ≪ is a partial order. Transitivity uses C6 to complete a diagram. Antisymmetry is reduced to a Lemma: if F ≼ K ≤ F, then K = F (a subdivision of a sub-figure K of F forces K = F).

This page.
1. He says the Lemma follows from C5 together with the corollary stated next, which he flags as a 'property of the relation ≤'.
2. Corollary (separation): let K ≤ F with K ≠ F. Then there is a non-empty figure G that is disjoint from K but not disjoint from F. Put differently, the sub-figure order is detected by disjointness: K ≤ F, and K is disjoint from no more than F is, together imply K = F.
3. He then notes that this is not 'formal' from axioms C1–C4 on (𝓕, ≤), and gives a counter-model:
   - Let 𝓕 be the lattice of closed subsets of an ordered set M, with the order (Alexandrov-type) topology.
   - Let 'disjoint' mean simply A ∩ B = ∅, so the compatibility relation is trivial.
   - Suppose M has a least element 0 and closed sets are down-closed. Then every non-empty closed set contains 0, so any two non-empty closed sets meet.
   - Hence the only G disjoint from a non-empty F is G = ∅. Replacing F by a proper non-empty closed K ⊂ F changes nothing.
   - The crossed-out instance is M = [0, N], F = M, K = [0, 1].
   - So separation fails.
4. The next page draws the conclusion. In this model, C6 for the relation ≼ on 𝓟_f(M) says only that F' ≼ F implies (F' empty iff F empty), and C6, C7 become tautological. So additional axioms are needed to secure the corollaries; he guesses the relevant axiom is the ⇒ part of 'Cont 4' (p. 35).

In modern terms, the corollary is a 'disjunction' or 'subfitness' condition on the lattice of figures. Classically, for closed sets of a T1 space it holds trivially: pick x ∈ F∖K, and {x} is closed and disjoint from K. It fails for non-T1 (Alexandrov / specialization-order) spaces, which is exactly the counterexample. The page thus serves the antisymmetry of refinement and identifies a missing separation axiom.
errors: No mathematical error. The counterexample is correct provided the closed sets are taken to be down-closed (so that every non-empty closed set contains 0). Grothendieck leaves this convention implicit.

As stated on the page, the corollary would have to be an extra axiom (or follow from later axioms such as Cont 4), since it is shown not to follow from C1–C4. The page therefore leaves the Lemma, and hence the antisymmetry of ≪, conditionally unproved.

ideas.what: Separation property: for a proper sub-figure K < F there is a non-empty G disjoint from K but meeting F. Equivalently, ≤ is determined by the disjointness relation.
ideas.modern_name: Wallman disjunction property / subfit (conjunctive) lattice or locale; separative poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Wallman (1938) for the disjunction property; Isbell and Simmons (1970s) for subfit locales

ideas.what: Counter-model to show non-formality: closed sets of an ordered set with least element (Alexandrov topology), where any two non-empty closed sets meet.
ideas.modern_name: Non-T1 Alexandrov space / specialization order; failure of subfitness

ideas.what: Refinement G ≪ F defined as the composite of sub-figure and subdivision (G ≤ F' ≼ F), with antisymmetry reduced to 'a subdivision of a sub-figure equal to the whole forces equality'.
ideas.modern_name: Order generated by two compatible preorders (factorization of morphisms into restriction followed by subdivision)
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; part of Grothendieck's own unpublished axiomatics of tame topology
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only announces a programme of 'topologie modérée', without these axioms

missed.claim: Grothendieck observes that his axioms C1–C7 on figures do not imply the separation (subfitness) property needed for antisymmetry of refinement, and leaves open which axiom (perhaps Cont 4 ⇒) should supply it. The axiom system for 'figures' in tame topology was never completed or published.
missed.quote: Ce n'est pas "formel" en termes de C1 à C4 sur (𝓕, ≤)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Anyone trying to reconstruct Grothendieck's axiomatic tame topology (for instance in relation to o-minimal structures) would need such a disjunction axiom. The page pinpoints that requirement, though the property itself is standard in point-free topology.

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful but routine axiomatic bookkeeping. The separation property he isolates is the classical Wallman disjunction / subfitness condition, and the counterexample is elementary. The only interest is as a glimpse of the unfinished axiomatics of the 1986 analysis situs notes.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 likely reads 'Cela résulte du corollaire qui suit, et de C5'.
'la relation de compatibilité de R[?]' is plausibly 'la relation de compatibilité étant la relation toujours vraie'. The 'R' is uncertain.
'remplace F par K∈F' should be read as 'remplace F par K ⊂ F' (K a proper closed subset); the K is overwritten in the image.
The crossed-out example reads 'M = [0, N], avec l'ordre habituel, F = M, K = [0, 1]'.
